description:
WOMEN SPRING SUMMER 2027
 
“An actress, after a day on set, takes the streets back to reality. The movie score lingers in her mind. 
The joy of dressing, the characters we write for ourselves, creating an illusion to captivate. When do we feel glamorous? 
These are things I had on my mind while working on this collection. I kept thinking about glamour, in quite an innocent way: the desire to feel done up, simply because you want to. And how charming that is.”

Julian Klausner

Discover the collection on driesvannoten.com

description:
MEN SPRING SUMMER 2027
 
“Early in the process, we stumbled on a book about L'Après-midi d'un faune, The Faun's Afternoon. The poem by Stéphane Mallarmé, from 1876, tells the story of a dream-like creature, half-man, half-animal, that wakes up from a nap in the woods. In his sleep he dreams of nymphs, sensually dancing.  He wakes up in a haze, confused about whether or not this actually happened. In the end, he decides to fall back asleep and ultimately chooses fantasy over reality.”

Julian Klausner

Discover the collection on driesvannoten.com

description:
We organised an art exhibition at the Hara Museum at the end of March in Tokyo to celebrate the 10th anniversary of our flagship store in Aoyama.
The concept of this exhibition was to reinterpret again the two huge paintings of the 17th century by three new young Japanese artists selected by Dries and exhibited their works at the Hara Museum just for three days.
Fashion Tsushin filmed the opening cocktail in the evening of the first day as well as the cocktail organised the next day at Dries Van Noten Aoyama store.
It is a short documentary of Dries’ stay in Tokyo. It aired on Fashion Tsushin in May.
title: Dries Van Noten celebrates 10th anniversary of flagship store in Aoyama

description:
Dries Van Noten
S/S 2015
 
An erudite Pre-Raphaelite.
Passionate of Arts and Crafts.
Barefoot in an early morning dewey pasture.
The romance and mystery of mid-summer's night.
A love of individual garments and a disregard for the conventions
of dressing and cover.
A warrior for love, a soaringly free spirit.
 
 
 
STRUCTURE:
Loose, floating, elongated, nonchalent, asymetric, layered, unconventional, defiant.
 
 
PRINTS:
Worldly, herbaceous, tradition revisited. colour block stripes, pixelated traditional motifs such as arc-typical Men's Neck-tie, bandana and pyjama patterns, a Cannabis leaf inspiration.
 
 
EMBROIDERY:
Festive, eclectic, figurative, hand embellishment, metals, ribbons, fraying and fringing.
 
FABRICS:
Diaphanous, translucent with opaque, Bloomsbury-esque silk brocades. Horta, Raw silk, silk chiffon, lurex, “summer fur” rainbow ribbons on organza, natural cottons, languid viscose.
 
 
 
 PALATE:
Kaleidoscopic, vivid, muted, keen, pigment, grass, earth..
 
 
 ACCESSORIES:
Sponge soled footwear reproduced in leathers and hide. Willowy twigs and roots reproduced in metals adorn necklines and wrists. Boob Tubes, a harness structure moulds the body. Clutches and holdalls in springbok and kangaroo. A bra. A cummerbund. 
 
SOUNDTRACK
Max Colombie AKA Oscar And The Wolf. A 23 year old Belgian musician and painter and a rendition of his summer festival hit Strange Entity.
